svg.title: How a run tells new metadata from new content
svg.desc: A document that was never exported is downloaded. For an exported document, a run compares the revision of Paperless with the one it saved. With a new revision, it asks Paperless for the checksum of the file, MD5 up to Paperless-ngx 2.x and SHA-256 since 3.0, and looks for it among the SHA-256 and the MD5 that it saved at the download. When the revision is the same, or the checksum is among them, the content is the same: the file stays where it is, or moves to its new path. When an earlier version of the app saved the SHA-256 alone and Paperless reports an MD5, the run computes both checksums of the mirrored file: when its SHA-256 is the saved one and its MD5 the one of Paperless, the content is the same too. Otherwise the run downloads the document to a temporary file, computes both checksums in one pass over it, writes it to Nextcloud in chunks, into the file of the document when it has one, which keeps its ID and moves to its new path first, and saves the checksums. The questions are indigo, the requests to Paperless-ngx green, and the results in Nextcloud blue.
